diagnostics.message: :module.forge_trust_validator_lambda: explicit depends_on of :resource.aws_cloudwatch_log_group.forge_trust_validator_lambda is redundant — already implied by attribute references
:resource.aws_cloudwatch_event_target.forge_trust_validator_lambda: explicit depends_on of :module.forge_trust_validator_lambda is redundant — already implied by attribute references

null_resource.update_forge_role_trust updates the forge roles' assume-role policy to trust the Lambda execution role "${var.prefix}-forge-trust-validator", which is created inside module.forge_trust_validator_lambda. Because the principal is built from var.prefix as a plain string (not a module attribute reference), Terraform cannot infer that the Lambda (and its IAM role) must exist before the trust policy is updated. On a fresh apply, the null_resource could run before the module and write a trust policy referencing a nonexistent role.

aws_cloudwatch_event_target.forge_trust_validator_lambda has an explicit depends_on on module.forge_trust_validator_lambda, but the dependency is already implied by the attribute reference in arn = module.forge_trust_validator_lambda.lambda_function_arn.

module.forge_trust_validator_lambda has an explicit depends_on on aws_cloudwatch_log_group.forge_trust_validator_lambda, but the dependency is already implied by logging_log_group = aws_cloudwatch_log_group.forge_trust_validator_lambda.name in the module's arguments.
